summary:
The Pangasinan provincial board certified and affirmed Municipal Ordinance No. 15, s-2023 of Bayambang protecting the rights of LGBTQI persons (Provincial Board Resolution No. 799-2024, session of 19 August 2024)—a provincial-level endorsement of a municipal LGBTQ+ protection ordinance in a conservative province. This gives a visitor in the Pangasinan corridor a local complaint route absent in most other regions.

Against that, the Abra and Ilocos Sur provinces within Ilocos Region host the Bodong Indigenous Allied Group (BIAG), a codified customary-justice system with its own dispute-resolution authority over "crimes and tribal-related offences," recognised by Philippine courts. No trans-specific bodong ruling or customary exclusion was documented, but the legal-pluralism structure means that in a rural Abra or Ilocos Sur dispute, the applicable institution may not be a Philippine court.

Net effect: +0.03 above the national score, modest because the protective ordinance is municipal and the plural-justice uncertainty is localized to specific provinces within the region. Compare Central Visayas (0.63), where the ordinance cluster is broader (city IRRs with UNDP backing, unanimous municipal votes) and there is no countervailing alternative-justice structure.

sources.summary: Certification of the Pangasinan Provincial Board (Sangguniang Panlalawigan), session of 19 August 2024: approves Resolution No. 799-2024 declaring Municipal Ordinance No. 15, s-2023 of the municipality of Bayambang — 'An Ordinance Protecting the Rights of Lesbians, Gays, Bisexuals, Transgenders, Queers and Intersex (LGBTQI) in the Municipality of Bayambang Against Any and All Forms of Discrimination Solely on the Basis of Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Expression, Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC)' — provincial-level affirmation of a municipal LGBTQI protection ordinance sponsored by board members Baniqued and Ventanilla.
